A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Koopman-CFM framework and authorship, despite the changed subtitle and substantial revision. All 22 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation results, sampling times, loss ablations, trajectory errors, and qualitative editing and image-restoration experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds quantitative semantic evaluations, inversion experiments, spectral analyses, training diagnostics, and scalability results.

M1.justification: The encoder, affine generator, decoder, four training losses, and one-step sampler are retained. However, v3 substantially extends the inference and control procedures with image-to-noise inversion, CLIP-ranked mode selection, CLIP-labeled class-mean editing directions, and backward transfer of those directions. It also introduces real-Schur analysis alongside eigenmode analysis; v2 primarily used canonical/eigenvector perturbations and mode un-lifting.

E1.justification: MNIST, FFHQ, and CIFAR-10 remain represented, including MNIST in v3's appendices. v3 adds an explicit real-image inversion task and expands semantic editing targets to attributes such as smile, age, and gender. Inpainting, super-resolution, and denoising were already evaluated in v2; diffusion and other modalities remain prospective.

E2.justification: The generation comparison replaces Consistency Flow Matching from v2 Table 1 with Rectified Flow and MeanFlow in v3 Table 7. OT-CFM and the without-consistency ablation remain. This substantially changes the one-step comparator set. Describing the ablation as equivalent to Berman et al. does not establish a separately evaluated additional baseline.

E3.justification: The existing Table 3 hyperparameters and 1,000-trajectory evaluation remain unchanged. Added protocols include FFHQ training at 64×64, extending the Koopman-dimension sweep to 2050, checkpoint comparisons at 20k/80k/160k steps, Schur-coordinate trajectory diagnostics, and CLIP-based coherence and CLIP/LPIPS editing evaluations. Table 8 specifies editing strength alpha = 3.0. These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v3 adds training-loss curves, component latency profiling, Schur-coordinate trajectory examples, progressive spectral reconstruction, class-conditioned spectra, teacher-training mode comparisons, and quantitative semantic and inversion analyses. It also expands scalability tests. The original loss ablations, trajectory MSE analysis, t-SNE visualization, and image-restoration examples are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v3 Table 4 newly reports latency values with plus/minus quantities, although their statistical meaning and repetition count are unspecified. The trajectory-error means, standard deviations, and 1,000-trajectory sample count already appear in v2 and are retained. Neither version provides explicit repeated-training seed information.

E6.justification: The generation table revises consistent-model CIFAR-10 FID from 17.4 to 16.7. The loss ablation changes consistent MNIST FID from 11.6 to 7.1 and changes CIFAR-10 without/with-consistency entries from 16.7/14.1 to 14.1/16.7. Reported Koopman sampling time changes from 0.4 to 37.2 ms/image; timing-protocol equivalence is undocumented, so this does not establish a same-setting slowdown. New results include FFHQ 64×64 FID 13.4, semantic scores, inversion outcomes, spectral findings, and deterioration at dimension 2050. The existing trajectory MSE statistics are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The three principal propositions and Appendix A proofs are retained, with corrected proof headings. v3 substantially extends the mathematical analysis through Schur-block dynamics and claimed mode independence, class spectral-response and coherence definitions, checkpoint-similarity measures, and truncated-basis reconstruction (Equations 14–20 and 26). Corollary 1.1 also removes v2's fixed-decoder condition, changing its stated assumptions.

C1.justification: Full-trajectory consistency, global Koopman linearization, and one-step sampling were already central claims in v2. v3 explicitly adds inversion and class-conditioned spectral signatures to the abstract's contributions and broadens claimed applicability beyond CFM velocity fields. It drops the abstract's dramatic-speedup claim and makes generation quality secondary to interpretability.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning coarse-to-fine generation, shared versus class-specific modes, progressive acquisition of teacher dynamics, and hair-color/illumination entanglement. It explicitly acknowledges that finite-dimensional representations are not guaranteed and that endpoint-pair generation remains necessary. It also introduces stronger assertions about valid transferred perturbations and attributes all learned-operator error to the teacher because the estimator is unbiased, an inference not established by the retained proof.

D1.justification: v3 adds a paper-code repository pointer, an explicit torchcfm source link, PyTorch implementation information, and a description of the matrix-exponential routine. It provides component timing information and additional procedural details for semantic editing and inversion. Existing architecture, hardware, and training-hyperparameter disclosures remain largely unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify repository availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations for MeanFlow, Consistency Trajectory Models, diffusion-training analyses by Biroli and Bonnaire, CLIP, and inversion methods, while removing some background references and Consistency Flow Matching. It sharpens the existing distinction from Berman et al. by identifying the without-consistency ablation with that approach. Numerous publication-year and venue updates concern retained works and do not constitute new positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the subtitle changes to Trajectory-Preserving Linearization. v3 introduces a dedicated interpretability/control section, reorganizes experiments around trajectory fidelity, moves generation-quality discussion into Appendix D, separates limitations from the conclusion, and reorganizes the appendices into spectral analysis and applications. These are substantial narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, the overview diagram is redrawn, and numerous diagnostic plots, semantic-editing grids, and quantitative tables are added. The dimension plot gains another point. Existing displays are also moved or reformatted: v2's t-SNE Figure 5 becomes v3 Figure 2, while the uncurated samples, decoded-mode comparison, and restoration examples remain present under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through broader baselines, quantitative semantic tests, inversion/scalability analyses, a code pointer, and reconciliation of several FID inconsistencies. However, Table 8 shows a CLIP–LPIPS tradeoff despite claiming improvement on both: CFM editing lowers LPIPS but also lowers CLIP. Sections 4.3 and 5.1 additionally assert that unbiased estimation excludes linearization error and that Schur modes evolve independently without establishing the required conditions. These gains and weaknesses both affect the central interpretability argument, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
